Kuvitus: uimahalli poikkileikkauksena. T: Illustration: a swimming hall in cross-section. In the background a tiled wall and tall windows. On the left, at the edge of the pool, is the lifeguard's tall chair, with a whistle hanging from its armrest. From the whistle, closely spaced arcs of wavefronts spread through the air towards the pool. On the right the pool seen from the side: water, a lane rope with floats on the surface and a dark lane marking on the bottom. Under the water the same wavefronts continue about four times farther apart.
Kaavakuva mittakaavassa: saman pillin ää: Diagram to scale: the sound of the same whistle as a pressure wave in air and in water, with a distance of one metre drawn equally long in both. Above, in air, the wavelength is 0.12 metres, so almost nine waves fit into a metre. Below, in water, the wavelength is 0.50 metres, and two waves fit into a metre. In both, one wavelength is marked with a bracket, and an arrow shows the direction of travel. The curve shows how the pressure varies. The frequency is the same in both, 3.0 kilohertz, but the speed of sound is about 350 metres per second in air and about 1500 in water.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: kolme seiso: Diagram, not to scale: three standing waves at the fundamental frequency one below the other, each of length L. At the top a string fixed at both ends: there is a node at each end and an antinode in the middle, and the length of the string is half the wavelength. In the middle a tube open at both ends: the displacement antinodes of the air are at the ends of the tube and the node in the middle, and the length of the tube is half the wavelength. At the bottom a tube closed at one end: there is a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end, and the length of the tube is a quarter of the wavelength.
Kuvaaja: heilurin jaksonaika T sekuntein: Graph: the period T of a pendulum in seconds as a function of the length l of the string in metres. Six black points at lengths 0.20–0.95 m, periods from 0.94 seconds to 1.98 seconds. A dashed curve that levels off runs through the points: four times the length gives only about twice the period, so no straight line through the origin fits the points.
Kuvaaja: jaksonajan neliö T toiseen seku: Graph: the square of the period, T squared, in seconds squared as a function of the length l of the string in metres. Six black points at lengths 0.20–0.95 m, values from 0.88 to 3.90. A rising straight line has been fitted to the points and extended as a dashed line to the vertical axis, which it crosses at about 0.055 s², a little above the origin. Two points on the line are circled, (0.10 m; 0.46 s²) and (0.90 m; 3.69 s²), from which the slope is read as about 4.04 s² per metre.
Käsitekartta. Ylhäällä solmu jaksollinen: Concept map. At the top the node periodic motion: period T, frequency f = 1 over T and amplitude A. Three branches lead down from it. Oscillators, repeating motion: spring force F = minus k x as vectors, period of the mass–spring oscillator T = 2 pi times the square root of m over k and period of the pendulum T = 2 pi times the square root of l over g. Waves, oscillation travels: the wave equation v = f lambda, constructive interference when the path difference is n lambda, and the natural frequencies of a string f n = n v over 2 L. Sound, a wave in air: beats f H = the absolute value of f 1 minus f 2, the Doppler effect for a source moving towards the observer and the intensity level L = 10 decibels times the logarithm of I over I 0.
